note: Set --ble-root to your local BLE project root before running. These evals test the REAL post-edit flow: a client-style change request is given (NO pre-staged .o artifacts, NO 'analyze the change' prompt), the harness runs ONE acceptEdits turn with the loci plugin loaded (flow='edit'), the pre-edit hook captures <basename>.o.prev BEFORE the Edit, Claude edits the real source, and the SessionStart auto-run rule fires loci-post-edit on its own — which is the behavior under test. The harness backs up and restores source_file so runs are hermetic. Each eval is a distinct, plausible field/customer request on a DIFFERENT function. All five target functions are confirmed present (NOT inlined) in CC2340R5/basic_ble.out, and all source files compile to a non-empty per-file .o: build-metadata discovers each file's real compile command via gmake-dry-run (confidence 'exact'), expanding build_components.opt so HOST_CONFIG/CENTRAL_CFG/PERIPHERAL_CFG are defined — verified by test-compiling app_connection.c (Connection_* symbols present) and hci.c (HCI_SendDataPkt present), so the #if(HOST_CONFIG…) guards in app_connection.c are NOT a blocker and no flags.json seeding is needed. Graded by grade_bash_post_edit: a '## Post-Edit:' header + 'Verdict: PASS|CAUTION|FAIL' line + a % diff (the pre-edit hook always captures a baseline in this flow). Two fields carry the claims this file used to make in prose only: `expect_baseline` fails a run whose report says it had no Before — which the note above asserts can never happen in this flow, and which the grader used to accept as a PASS — and `expect_no_change` (pe-13) fails a run that invents a delta for an edit-and-revert turn whose net effect on the object is nothing. FIXTURE: every eval here names `examples/rtos/LP_EM_CC2340R53/.../basic_ble_profiles/...` and `$LOCI_TEST_BLE_ROOT/CC2340R5/basic_ble.out`. That is one particular BLE checkout — a tree laid out as `LP_EM_CC2340R5/.../basic_ble/` with no top-level `CC2340R5/` image will ERROR with `source_file missing or not found` before the model is ever asked anything. Repointing the paths is not a rename: the note above records that each target function was verified PRESENT and not inlined in that image, and that each file compiles to a non-empty per-file object, so a new tree has to be re-verified the same way before its paths go in here.

evals.prompt: A field customer reports their peripheral keeps renegotiating its connection MTU and they want to quantify how often it happens. In $LOCI_TEST_BLE_ROOT/examples/rtos/LP_EM_CC2340R53/ble5stack/basic_ble_profiles/app/app_data.c, update GATT_EventHandler so it keeps a running count of ATT MTU update events and includes that cumulative count in the status message it already prints on an MTU update. The data module is compiled into $LOCI_TEST_BLE_ROOT/CC2340R5/basic_ble.out.
evals.expected_output: No pre-staged artifacts and no 'analyze' instruction are given — Claude edits app_data.c directly to add the MTU-update counter. The pre-edit hook captures app_data.o.prev before the Edit; after the edit lands, loci-post-edit auto-fires WITHOUT being asked: it runs diff-elfs on app_data.o.prev vs app_data.o, identifies GATT_EventHandler as modified, extracts pre/post assembly, calls the LOCI MCP for pre and post timing, and emits the Step 6 conclusion table headed '## Post-Edit: GATT_EventHandler' with a Performance row (Before/After execution_time_ns and ±% in the Note) and an Energy row, closing with a 'Verdict: **PASS|CAUTION|FAIL**' line and the 'LOCI post-edit · …' footer.

evals.prompt: In $LOCI_TEST_BLE_ROOT/examples/rtos/LP_EM_CC2340R53/ble5stack/basic_ble_profiles/app/app_data.c, change the ATT MTU status message in GATT_EventHandler to read "MTU updated" instead of whatever it says now. Then reconsider: the original wording is the one the field team greps for, so put it back exactly as it was. Use the Edit tool for both changes.
evals.expected_output: Two edits land in ONE turn and their net effect on the compiled object is nothing. The pre-edit hook captures app_data.o.prev before the FIRST edit and keeps it for the second (first-write-wins per turn), so the Before side is the state of the file before either change — not the state after the first. loci-post-edit therefore compares the rebuilt object against a baseline it is identical to, `loci elf diff` reports no changed functions, and the report SAYS the object is unchanged rather than reporting a timing delta. A report carrying a signed % change here is wrong twice over: the number is fabricated, and it can only have come from a baseline that moved with the first edit.

The report does NOT present a signed percentage timing or energy delta
The report does NOT claim it had no pre-edit baseline
